observations: Photo 0 shows the control panel with 'PSR-540' and 'YAMAHA' branding, a 'FLOPPY DISC DRIVE' sticker, and '2 CHANNEL SYSTEM' text.
Photo 1 shows the top of the keyboard with a green LCD screen, a 'YAMAHA' logo, and a '2 CHANNEL SYSTEM' label.
Photo 2 shows the keyboard keys and a 'YAMAHA' logo on the right side.
The seller's text mentions a 'first body' and 'working perfect pitch bend', but these are not visible in the photos.
The photos are blurry and show significant wear on the keys and the keyboard surface.

claims.evidence: photo 0 shows the brand and model on the control panel.
The physical condition of the keyboard body is not shown.
No photo shows this feature in operation.
photo 1 and photo 2 show the '2 CHANNEL SYSTEM' label.
The LCD screen is visible but the image quality is poor in all photos.

claims.claim: All keys and buttons working, adapter included. Bought from the UK, no dead key, no crackle.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The keyboard may not power on or produce sound.
risks.proof: A video of the keyboard being played.

risks.risk: The LCD screen may be cracked or have dead pixels.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the screen while powered on.

risks.risk: The pitch bend wheel may be faulty.
risks.proof: A video showing the wheel being used to change pitch.
risks.if_unproven: as having a broken pitch bend wheel

risks.risk: The internal battery may be dead.
risks.proof: A video showing the keyboard playing music without a power source.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Video of the keyboard powered on and playing music.
Clear photo of the LCD screen while the keyboard is running.
Video showing the pitch bend wheel in action.
Photo of the keyboard with the power switch and battery compartment open.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
